title: Festival Countdown
guardrail: Made-up prices. Real life is different.

masti.for: Mela plans and the ring toss

intro.pick: Which festival is your family getting ready for?
intro.line1: Three days to the festival! Here is {{money}} for everything.
intro.line2: First, my list. Then something nice for yourself and your friends. And keep your bus fare.
intro.hint: Oh, and Mamu's family might visit this year.

planner.title: Plan your money
planner.sub: Drag coins into pockets, or use − and +. Whatever you don't place stays as loose change.
planner.subLater: Moving money now is planning, not raiding. It's free.
planner.ayesha: Keep a little loose change. Something always comes up during festivals.
planner.busNeeded: Put at least ₹20 in Bus fare to get home tonight.
planner.tired: You walked home last night. You're tired: only {{n}} stall visits today.
planner.ayeshaRepaid: Ayesha paid back your ₹20, like she said.

panipuri.text: Your turn to treat us to pani puri!

biryani.text: Biryani at the big stall! Coming?

loan.text: Lend me ₹100? I'll pay you back tomorrow, promise.

ride.text: The big ride! Last night of the mela!

selfie.text: Selfie booth? We split it three ways.

covers.text: Light-up phone covers! We all get one?

ayesha.text: I spent my bus money. Can you cover ₹20?

ring.title: Ring toss
ring.sign: 3 rings for ₹30. Win the giant teddy!
ring.odds: About 1 in 12 players wins. On average, each try costs you about ₹28.

mamu.title: Surprise!
mamu.text: Mamu's family just arrived! We need snacks.

needs.l1: You spent {{m}} at the mela and the {{item}} is still not bought.
needs.l2: Needs keep the family going; wants are extra.
needs.more: A need is something the family can't do the festival without. A want makes it more fun. Both matter, but when money runs short, the needs go first.

budget.l2: A budget only works if each pocket does its job.
budget.l3: Plan it, then stick to it.
budget.more: A budget is a plan that gives every rupee a job before you spend it. Moving money later is fine sometimes, but if it happens a lot, the plan isn't really a plan.

opportunity.l1: The mela took {{r}} from Ammi's gift.
opportunity.l2: Every rupee spent is a rupee not spent on something else.
opportunity.more: The real cost of a choice is the best thing you gave up to make it. Here, a fun evening cost part of a gift.

compare.l2: Prices differ a lot for the same thing.
compare.more: The same item can cost very different amounts in shops a few steps apart. Looking at two or three before buying usually saves money.

cheap.l1: The {{cheap}} outfit tore; the new one cost {{new}}.
cheap.l2: Low price, low quality can mean paying twice.
cheap.more: Something cheap that breaks quickly can cost more than something a little dearer that lasts.

early.l1: Buying the {{item}} on day {{d}} cost {{extra}} more.
early.more: When everyone wants the same thing at the same time, prices go up. Planning early lets you buy before the rush.

fakesale.l1: "50% off" was still {{extra}} above Daam Fix.
fakesale.l2: A sale price can be a raised price, cut.
fakesale.l3: Compare the price, not the discount.
fakesale.more: A big "was" price makes any price look small. What matters is what you pay compared with other shops, not the percentage on the sign.

buffer.good: Your loose change covered Mamu's visit.
buffer.more: A buffer is money with no job yet, kept for the things you can't predict. When a surprise comes, it stops you from breaking your plan.

swap.l1: You swapped {{n}} plans and kept your friends happy.
swap.l2: Cheaper plans can be just as fun.
swap.more: You don't have to choose between your wallet and your friends. Suggesting a cheaper plan keeps both.

odds.l1: You spent {{x}} at the ring toss.
odds.l2: Games of chance are built so most players lose.
odds.l3: If the odds are hidden, walk away.
odds.more: Stalls and games of chance are designed so they earn more than they pay out. Over many tries, players lose on average.

tips.plan: keep loose change and bus fare safe
